Resolve files via `new URL('../public/index.html', import.meta.url)`. ## Part 1: static HTML checks (read index.html as text, regex-based) - `` text and the only `<h1>` text are `Room bookings` (exactly one h1). - `<form id="booking-form" ...>` has `novalidate` attribute. - Inside the form (substring between `<form` and `</form>`): select#room name=room; input type=text id=title name=title; input type=date id=date name=date; input type=time id=start / id=end with names; `<button type="submit" id="book">Book</button>`. - For each of room/title/date/start/end/filter-date: a `<label for="X">TEXT</label>` with exact text (Room, Title, Date, Start, End, Show date) and the label's inner content contains no `<` (so it does not contain the field). - Outside the form: input type=date id=filter-date; `<button type="button" id="show-all">Show all</button>`; `<ul id="booking-list">`; `<p id="error" role="alert"></p>` empty. - Last element in body: the text right before `</body>` (trimmed) ends with `<script src="/app.js"></script>`; that script tag has no type/defer/async; there is exactly one `<script` in the file (no inline script). - No `<option`, none of `Aurora`, `Borealis`, `Cosmos`; no ` on[a-z]+=` attributes; neither index.html nor app.js contains `http://` or `https://`. - app.js contains no `import`/`export` statements (regex `^\s*(import|export)\b` multiline). ## Part 2: behavioural tests with node:vm Build a fake DOM where the APP only sees allowed APIs, enforced with Proxies that THROW on any other property get/set: - Element internal state (test-side): `{ tag, id, children: [], listeners: {type: [fn]}, value: '', type: '', disabled: false }`. Text nodes are `{ text: '...' }` objects (`isText`). - App-facing element = Proxy over the internal allowing get of: `textContent`, `value`, `type`, `disabled`, `append`, `replaceChildren`, `addEventListener`; set of: `textContent`, `value`, `type`, `disabled`. Anything else (e.g. `innerHTML`, `appendChild`, `children`, `dispatchEvent`) throws Error('forbidden: ' + prop). Allow get of `then` returning undefined? No — just make sure the Proxy never gets awaited; if needed allow symbol props (Symbol.toPrimitive etc.) to return undefined. - `textContent` get = concatenation of descendant text; set = children replaced by one text node (empty string → no children). `append(...args)`: strings become text nodes, proxied elements are mapped back to their internal (keep a WeakMap proxy→internal). `replaceChildren(...args)` same but replaces. - `document` Proxy: only `getElementById(id)` (returns the pre-built element proxies for: booking-form, room, title, date, start, end, book, filter-date, show-all, booking-list, error; null otherwise) and `createElement(tag)`. - Event objects passed to listeners: Proxy allowing only `preventDefault` (records a flag). - `fetch(url, options)`: records `{url, options}` in a calls array and returns a promise the test resolves/rejects manually (deferred). Helpers: `respond(call, status, body)` resolves with a response Proxy exposing only `status` and `json()`; json() returns Promise resolving to a structured clone of body; `respondBadJson(call, status)` where json() rejects; `fail(call)` rejects fetch with TypeError. Track whether json() was called (for 204 test). - Context: `vm.createContext({ document, fetch })` only (no window/console). Run app.js source with `vm.runInContext(src, ctx)`. - Flush helper: `await new Promise(r => setImmediate(r))` a few times. - Dispatch helper (test side): call listeners of internal element for a type with a fake event. - Inspect helpers: list items = internal booking-list children; each li children; error text. - Elements' `value` for the form fields is set by tests on the internal state before submitting. Test cases (each a separate `test`, fresh page per test): 1. On load, exactly two fetches start synchronously (before any flush): `/api/rooms` and `/api/bookings`, both method GET (options.method may be 'GET' or absent — accept either), list fetch does not wait for rooms. 2. Rooms 200 `{rooms:['Aurora','Borealis','Cosmos']}` → #room has 3 option elements in order, each value and textContent equal to the name; #error stays ''. 3. Rooms error 500 `{error:'internal error'}` → #error 'internal error', #room empty. Rooms error with body `{error: 5}` → 'Request failed.'; with body `['x']` → 'Request failed.'; with body null → 'Request failed.'. 4. Rooms network failure → 'Could not reach the server.', #room empty. Rooms 200 with bad JSON → 'Could not reach the server.'. 5. List rendering: bookings `[{id:1,room:'Aurora',title:'Standup',date:'2026-11-03',start:'09:00',end:'10:00'}, {id:2,room:'Cosmos',title:'<b>x</b>',...}]` → 2 li; each li has exactly 2 children; first is text node with exact text `2026-11-03 09:00-10:00 Aurora: Standup`; second is element tag 'button' with type 'button' and textContent 'Cancel'; the second li's text contains literal `<b>x</b>` as a text node (no element children besides button). 6. Empty list → single li whose only child is text node 'No bookings.'. 7. List error after a successful render: render one booking, then trigger refetch (change event on filter), respond 400 `{error:'date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date'}` → #error shows it, list unchanged. Same with network failure → 'Could not reach the server.', list unchanged. A successful list fetch leaves an existing #error text alone (set error via rooms failure first). 8. Filter: set filter value '2026-11-03', dispatch 'change' → new fetch `/api/bookings?date=2026-11-03`; dispatch 'input' → no new fetch. Value with weird chars e.g. 'a b&c' is appended unchanged: `/api/bookings?date=a b&c`. 9. Overlapping list fetches: start A (load) and B (change). Resolve B with one booking, then resolve A with a different list → list shows B's. Also: A rejects / A returns 500 after B succeeded → #error stays '' and list stays B's. Also A resolved first while B pending → list unchanged (still initial empty-children) and error unchanged; then B resolves → applied. 10. Show all: filter value '2026-11-03', click show-all → filter value '' and exactly one new fetch `/api/bookings`; no change/input listeners invoked (spy by wrapping: check that the number of fetches increased by exactly 1). 11. Submit happy path: set room 'Aurora', title ' Standup ', date, start, end; dispatch submit → preventDefault called; book.disabled true; one POST call to `/api/bookings` with options.method 'POST', options.headers deep-equal `{'Content-Type':'application/json'}` (exactly that one key), JSON.parse(options.body) deep-equal the five values unchanged (title untrimmed) with exactly those 5 keys. Second submit while disabled → preventDefault still called, no new fetch. Respond 201 with the booking → after flush: book.disabled false, title value '', other fields unchanged, #error '' (set it non-empty before), and a new GET `/api/bookings` list fetch started. 12. Re-enable timing: make json() for the POST reply return a deferred promise you control; after respond + flush but before json resolves, book still disabled; after json resolves, disabled false. 13. Submit error 409 `{error:'room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00'}` → #error exact message, book enabled, title kept, no new list fetch. Submit network failure → 'Could not reach the server.', book enabled, no list fetch. Submit 201 with bad JSON → 'Could not reach the server.', title kept, no list fetch. 14. Cancel: render a booking id 7; click its Cancel → button.disabled true, DELETE call url `/api/bookings/7` method 'DELETE'. Respond 204 (json must NOT be called) → button enabled, #error '' (pre-set non-empty), new list fetch. Respond 404 `{error:'booking not found'}` → #error 'booking not found', button enabled, list refetch. Network failure → 'Could not reach the server.', button enabled, NO list refetch. 404 with bad JSON → 'Could not reach the server.', no refetch. 15. Forbidden-API guard sanity: a tiny script run in the same fake context that does `document.body` or `el.innerHTML = 'x'` throws (proves the fakes enforce the allowlist). content.content: 1 # Full spec (verbatim from the user; final, no questions possible) 2 3 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). 4 5 Server 6 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 7 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 8 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 9 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 10 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 11 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 14 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 15 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 16 17 API 18 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 19 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 22 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 23 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. Other query parameters are ignored. 24 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 25 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. 26 - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). 27 - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. 29 - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. 30 31 Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 32 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 33 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 34 3. I wrote the two test files, but I couldn't run them. The Bash tool was denied permission, so I never ran `node --test test/app.test.mjs`. I haven't seen a pass or fail, and I haven't looked for bugs in `app.js` by running anything.

**Files created**
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-a87b97bc/test/app-fake-dom.mjs` is the helper module, about 150 lines. It has the Proxy-guarded fake elements, `document`, `fetch`, `respond`, `respondBadJson`, `fail`, `flush`, `dispatch` and `deferred`. It runs `app.js` with `vm.createContext({ document, fetch })` only.
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-a87b97bc/test/app.test.mjs` is the test file, about 330 lines, under the 600-line limit.

I did not edit `public/index.html` or `public/app.js`.

**What the tests cover**
- Part 1 has 6 static checks on `index.html` and `app.js`.
- Part 2 has the behavioural tests 1–15 from your list. Tests 14 and 15 are split into several `test` calls. I also added a trivial helper sanity test.
- That makes about 24 tests in total.

**Things to know when you run it**
- **Unused helper:** the trivial helper sanity test only exists to use `listCalls`. If you prefer, delete both.
- **`app.js` behaviour:** reading `app.js` against the spec, I found nothing I'd call a bug.
- **Spec gap:** a 204 reply to the POST or a GET counts as an error status with the "Request failed." message. That fits the spec, but no test covers it.
